extracted.intended_audience: patent AI researchers, NLP researchers working on patents, and computational linguists interested in automated patent examination
extracted.subtask_description: Creation and evaluation of a dataset (PEDANTIC) of US patent claims annotated with reasons for indefiniteness, using an automatic pipeline (USPTO office action retrieval + LLM extraction) with human validation and novel evaluation methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definiteness / Indefiniteness (35 U.S.C §112(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent claims define the scope of protection for an invention. If there are ambiguities in a claim, it is rejected by the patent office. In the US, this is referred to as indefiniteness (35 U.S.C § 112(b)) and is among the most frequent reasons for patent application rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims must avoid ambiguity; meeting the definiteness requirement under 35 U.S.C. §112(b) is essential to prevent rejection. Use examiner reasons for indefiniteness as the operative legal/administrative standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of USPTO office actions as source of examiner-cited reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: The dataset construction retrieves office action documents from the USPTO and uses those documents to identify and extract reasons for indefiniteness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office actions are treated as the ground-truth source of examiner-cited reasons; any automatic extraction or annotation pipeline should reliably locate and parse these documents to capture the specific examiner rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation pipeline quality: automatic extraction plus human validation
rubrics_metrics.description: PEDANTIC is constructed using a fully automatic pipeline that retrieves office actions and uses Large Language Models (LLMs) to extract the reasons for indefiniteness. A human validation study confirms the pipeline's accuracy in generating high-quality annotations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine automatic (LLM-based) extraction with human validation to ensure annotation accuracy. Report validation results and error rates to justify dataset quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation beyond binary classification metrics (LLM-as-Judge reason-level comparison)
rubrics_metrics.description: To gain insight beyond binary classification metrics, the authors implement an LLM-as-Judge evaluation that compares the free-form reasoning of every model-cited reason with every examiner-cited reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating models on definiteness, include reason-level, free-form comparison (e.g., via an LLM judge) rather than relying solely on binary label accuracy; this reveals whether models identify underlying reasons even if overall classification metrics are similar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset design: domain restriction and scale
rubrics_metrics.description: PEDANTIC is a novel dataset of 14k US patent claims from patent applications relating to Natural Language Processing (NLP), annotated with reasons for indefiniteness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curate datasets with clear scope (e.g., domain-limited to NLP-related claims) and sufficient scale (thousands of examples) to support model training and evaluation; document selection criteria and domain focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open release and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors state: 'We will publicly release the dataset and code.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Release dataset and code publicly to enable reproducibility and further research; include pipeline code, retrieval methods, and validation procedures.
